title: data-region-onboarding-sprint-notes-wildcard-exceptions
content:
Context:
This is a working log for the upcoming sprint focused on onboarding customers that present mixed-territory requirements (per-country anchors + selective global fallthrough). The emphasis here is on handling wildcard/temporary exceptions (legal waivers, partner-hosted assets) while keeping telemetry and operator-safety guarantees intact.

Goal:
- Deliver an onboarding checklist and automation recipe that reduces manual triage for exception cases by 60%
- Define telemetry and acceptance criteria so SRE/Support can detect leakage or incorrect routing within 5 minutes
- Produce contract checklist bits (DPA addendum snippets) that Sales/Legal can use during negotiation

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Customer onboarding flow for mixed-region tenancy (per-tenant country anchors with optional cross-border fallthrough bands)
- Wildcard exception handling: temporary country waivers, third-party subprocessors, IP-based ambiguity windows
- Operator checklist, acceptance tests, telemetry signals, rollback and remediation playbooks

Non-goals:
- Deep design of pinning algorithm kernels (that lives in routing team RFC)
- Changes to billing model or rate-limits

High-level approach:
1) Preflight: intake form + automated evidence collector
   - Intake form fields: declared territories, subprocessors list, sample SLO/latency needs, copy of relevant contract clause
   - Automated evidence collector runs a synthetic routing trace (10 sample request vectors from customer's major IP blocks) and returns a routing footprint heatmap

2) Policy synthesis: generate a draft policy for the tenant combining declared territories + inferred hotspots
   - Policy includes: primary anchor country, allowed fallthrough countries (ordered priority), hard-exceptions (never route), exception TTL if temporary
   - Output is a machine-readable policy YAML that the operator can review

3) Canary + audit: staged rollout with telemetry gates
   - 1% traffic -> metrics and evidence capture (full request headers, geo-decisions, matched-policy-id) retained for 14 days in secure log store
   - Gate criteria: no more than 0.1% of requests violating hard-exceptions; average geo-decision-latency < 20ms; no PII leakage to non-anchors (see telemetry signals)

Wildcard/Temporary Exception Workflow (distinct flow):
- Use case: Customer signs a temporary waiver allowing specific third-party subprocessor (e.g., partner analytics in Country X) for 90 days while they migrate data flows.
- Implementation notes:
  - Exceptions are issued as timeboxed policy overlays (policy-overlay://<tenant>/<overlay-id>) with TTL and required attestation document attached.
  - Overlay creation requires: Legal approval (email key), Security review (checklist), and an Ops ticket with runbook link.
  - System enforces last-mile evidence collection: every request that matches the overlay must include a short evidence token (signed by ingest proxy) preserved for audits.

Operator Acceptance Checklist (pre-roll):
- Intake form completed and evidence heatmap attached
- Policy YAML approved by customer contact and Legal (email thread saved)
- Canary automation job configured (1%, 5%, 25% stages) and scheduled
- Telemetry retention policy set to 14 days for the tenant audit logs
- Backup routing plan (fallback to nearest-compliant-region) preconfigured and smoke-tested

Telemetry signals to monitor (alerts + dashboards):
- geo-route-decision.count (by policy-id, by country) - count and delta over 1m/5m
- geo-route-violation.count (hard-exception matches) - immediate P0 alert if > 5/min across tenant
- evidence-missing.rate (requests where overlay token not found) - P1 if > 0.5%
- geo-decision-latency.p50/p95/p99 - target p95 < 100ms for onboarding canary
- cross-region-egress.bytes (by tenant) - used to estimate cost exposure for legal
- sample-leakage-scan.matches (run daily) - periodic job that inspects sample payloads for obvious country-specific PII markers

Canary test cases (automated):
- TC1: declared-anchor-country = FR; synthetic client IPs from FR, DE, US -> ensure FR hits, DE falls back to EU anchor, US routes to global fallthrough only if overlay present
- TC2: overlay present for third-party in IE (90d TTL) -> requests matching overlay must contain overlay evidence token; verify token, verify logs retained
- TC3: network partition (simulate EU region outage) -> check fallback to next-compliant-region respects hard-exceptions and that operator receives escalation ticket automatically

Rollback & Remediation Playbook:
- Automated rollback trigger: Any P0 alert firing during canary -> immediate rollback to previous policy for that tenant and create a high-priority incident ticket
- Manual rollback steps: toggle tenant policy to "enforced: previous" via admin console, run smoke trace, confirm evidence retention is restored
- Postmortem scope: routing decision traces, operator chat logs, legal communications, and sample payloads (redacted)

Legal and Sales checklist (DPA / Contract snippets):
- Required: clause that specifies permitted subprocessors and whether temporary exceptions require written addendum or single email attestation
- Suggested: Add TTL for exception (max 180 days by default) and automatic expiry unless renewed
- Evidence preservation clause: Redwood to preserve per-request overlay tokens for audit retention window (14 days default, can be extended by request)

Unresolved questions + risks:
- IP-to-country false positives in mobile + VPN-heavy customers (we should add a risk flag in intake form and select stronger evidence requirements)
- Long-tail cost for cross-region egress when many exceptions accumulate - need cost analytics hook in onboarding flow
- Legal: who signs temporary exception attestation for enterprise customers (primary signatory vs delegated admin)?

Sprint deliverables (2 weeks):
- Week 1: intake form v0, policy YAML template, synthetic trace harness and heatmap output
- Week 2: overlay proto (create/approve/revoke), canary automation job template, telemetry dashboard mock

Quick links / refs (working):
- CONFC-4821 (policy contract templates)
- JIRA-PRIV-917 (overlay implementation epic)
- github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/region-routing/pull/243 (initial overlay schema)

Notes to self / reminders:
- Coordinate with Billing on cross-region egress tagging for exceptions (Marisol)
- Add ingestion-proxy evidence token schema to security checklist (Ken)
- Get Legal to sign off on 90d-vs-180d default TTL and update onboarding docs

If you step through the canary plan and the telemetry gates fail, escalate to the "territory-exceptions-oncall" rota and preserve the full sample logs before rollback. This doc is a working draft — please add comments inline or attach Slack thread #priv-deploy-exceptions for discussion.
